chunks: And it was reported as well, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira,

and he explained them: in the Dhuhr prayer there are twenty-one takbirations, and in the Asr prayer there are twenty-one takbirations, and in the Maghrib prayer there are sixteen takbirations, and in the last Isha prayer there are twenty-one takbirations, and in the Fajr prayer there are eleven takbirations, and there are five takbirations of the Qunut in the five prayers.

key_terms.الصَّلَوَات: The prayers (specifically the five daily obligatory prayers)

ai.seo_question: How many takbirations are recited in each of the five daily prayers according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi outlines the specific number of takbirations for each of the five daily prayers, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential view that the takbirat al-ihram is supplemented by additional takbirations during the standing (qiyam) phase. The text highlights a distinct count for each prayer—such as twenty-one for Dhuhr and Asr, and sixteen for Maghrib—while also specifying five takbirations for the Qunut in each prayer, underscoring the ritual precision emphasized in Imami fiqh.
